title: Water Moves Toward More Dissolved Salt

scenes.tts: Sprinkle salt on cucumber slices. In about fifteen minutes, drops of water bead up on top. Put limp lettuce in plain cold water. In about fifteen minutes, it can turn crisp again. Nobody pushes the water, and the cells do not pump it. So how does it move, and which way?
scenes.visual: Cucumber slice gets salt and beads of water; limp lettuce in a bowl straightens; two question boxes appear.
scenes.narration: Sprinkle salt on cucumber slices. In about fifteen minutes, drops of water bead up on top. Put limp lettuce in plain cold water. In about fifteen minutes, it can turn crisp again. Nobody pushes the water, and the cells do not pump it. So how does it move, and which way?

scenes.tts: Drop food colouring into still water. At first, it sits in one spot. Concentration is how much of a substance is in a given space. Where the drop landed, the dye is highly concentrated. Far away, it is low. The particles are always moving at random. More leave the crowded spot than enter it. So the dye spreads.
scenes.visual: Glass with a cluster of dye dots that random-walks out until evenly spread; high and low labels.
scenes.narration: Drop food colouring into still water. At first, it sits in one spot. Concentration is how much of a substance is in a given space. Where the drop landed, the dye is highly concentrated. Far away, it is low. The particles are always moving at random. More leave the crowded spot than enter it. So the dye spreads.

scenes.tts: Diffusion is the movement of a substance from where it is more concentrated to where it is less concentrated. Now the dye is even. The particles do not stop. Just as many move one way as the other. So the colour stops changing.
scenes.visual: Diffusion chip with arrow high to low; evenly spread dots keep jiggling with two equal arrows.
scenes.narration: Diffusion is the movement of a substance from where it is more concentrated to where it is less concentrated. Now the dye is even. The particles do not stop. Just as many move one way as the other. So the colour stops changing.

scenes.tts: The cell membrane is the thin layer around every cell. It is selectively permeable. It lets some things through and holds back others. Water, oxygen and carbon dioxide cross easily. Many dissolved particles, such as salt and sugar, cross much less easily. Oxygen is more concentrated in the blood than inside a cell, so it diffuses in.
scenes.visual: Dashed membrane between blood and cell; water crosses, salt bounces back, oxygen moves from more to fewer.
scenes.narration: The cell membrane is the thin layer around every cell. It is selectively permeable. It lets some things through and holds back others. Water, oxygen and carbon dioxide cross easily. Many dissolved particles, such as salt and sugar, cross much less easily. Oxygen is more concentrated in the blood than inside a cell, so it diffuses in.

scenes.tts: Osmosis is the movement of water across a cell membrane. Dissolve salt in water, and the water there is less concentrated. Water moves toward the side with more dissolved salt. Many dissolved particles cannot follow, so the water keeps moving that way. Our model membrane holds back all the salt. Real ones let some through, much more slowly.
scenes.visual: Plain water left, salty water right; net water crossing to the salty side and its level rising.
scenes.narration: Osmosis is the movement of water across a cell membrane. Dissolve salt in water, and the water there is less concentrated. Water moves toward the side with more dissolved salt. Many dissolved particles cannot follow, so the water keeps moving that way. Our model membrane holds back all the salt. Real ones let some through, much more slowly.

scenes.tts: Now the cucumber makes sense. Salt outside means the water outside is less concentrated, so water leaves the cells. In lettuce, each cell holds more dissolved particles than plain water, so water moves in. Neither time do the cells spend energy. That is passive transport. Water moves toward more dissolved particles, and the cell spends no energy.
scenes.visual: Cucumber cell loses water to salty outside; lettuce cell gains water from plain water; passive transport chip.
